description: Modeling bounds and abstractions: each states its bound, why the bounded property is safe, and how to lift it.
modeled_scope: Five paths in two roots, three content hashes, and small mtime/len values; intake lanes are collapsed onto one set; each worker step is atomic; direct API writes that bypass the intake (ApiRemove, ApiMove, ApiAssignDirMove, AppSidecarEdit, RotateImage, ExternalRenameDir) are synchronous, while ApiUpload stores the file and fire-and-forget enqueues intake; crashes occur between completed durable writes; directory paths are flat fixed pairs. Not modeled: watcher delivery, general liveness, partial durable writes, and hierarchical directory paths.

scopes.title: Initial converged state
scopes.bound: Every run starts from fully matching files and rows (initialFile, initialRow, init in utils/quint/pipeline/eventual-consistency-state.qnt).
scopes.why_safe: Convergence is about healing divergence, so runs introduce divergence explicitly before asserting the heal.
scopes.lifting: Start runs from arbitrary states (not yet modeled).

scopes.title: Finite bounds
scopes.bound: Five paths, three content hashes, three small mtime/len values (PATHS, HASHES, SMALL in utils/quint/pipeline/eventual-consistency-state.qnt).
scopes.why_safe: The properties checked (identity match, no lost intake, no permanent staleness) are per-path and pairwise; bounds are sized to exhibit every guard outcome (match, mismatch, superseded, stale, missing) and to hold one two-asset subtree move plus a second sweep root.
scopes.lifting: Bound-escalation runs at larger sizes (not yet modeled).

scopes.title: Collapsed intake lanes
scopes.bound: The five intake lanes ride one intake set; priority scheduling is not modeled (see the intake comment in utils/quint/pipeline/eventual-consistency.qnt).
scopes.why_safe: No checked property depends on lane order — guards are per-item (generation, snapshot), never positional.
scopes.lifting: Lane-aware scheduling with fairness properties (explicitly out of scope; Apalache/TLC stay out as well).

scopes.title: Atomic worker step
scopes.bound: Each worker action (WorkerApply*, skips, removes) applies in one step; there are no open/hash/apply micro-stages, so no modify-during-pipeline interleaving exists in the model.
scopes.why_safe: The hash-to-skip re-stat window is the only guarded window in code; the open-to-hash window is unguarded there too — the model matches the implementation's actual guarantee, not a stronger one.

scopes.title: Synchronous direct writes
scopes.bound: Actions that write the projection without the intake (ApiRemove, ApiMove, ApiAssignDirMove, AppSidecarEdit, RotateImage, ExternalRenameDir) apply in the same step as their filesystem effect, with no writer inbox (see the direct-write comment in utils/quint/pipeline/eventual-consistency.qnt). ApiUpload is excluded: it stores the file and fire-and-forget enqueues intake (submit_uploaded_path -> submit_watcher_index), so the projection write happens later in the worker.
scopes.why_safe: The model proves convergence given synchronous writes; the lag between acknowledgment and visibility is a known divergence, tracked as an open fault rather than assumed away. ApiUpload no longer writes the projection synchronously, so its visibility lag is the by-design unindexed window (N8) rather than a barrier fault.
scopes.lifting: A writerInbox pending state mirroring the serial writer.

scopes.title: Completed-write crash abstraction
scopes.bound: Crash and DB-loss actions occur between completed durable writes: the model never represents a partially written row or sidecar (PROCESS_CRASH drops volatile intake; DB_LOSS clears the row map; DERIVED_STORE_LOSS clears thumbnail flags).
scopes.why_safe: The recovery runs assert convergence from every interrupted state the model represents (queue lost, rows cleared, thumbnails lost, sidecar ahead of row), so the proof does not lean on partial-write behaviour; store transaction durability is a property of redb, outside this model.
scopes.lifting: Model partial durable writes and store transactions explicitly.

scopes.title: Flat directory paths
scopes.bound: Path IDs carry no directory hierarchy. A directory rename is a fixed finite set of path pairs (SUBTREE_PAIRS in utils/quint/pipeline/eventual-consistency.qnt) moved atomically; arbitrary subtrees are not modeled.
scopes.why_safe: The property under proof is per-descendant row/path consistency plus all-or-nothing row updates, which a fixed two-asset pair set exhibits at the model's bounds.
scopes.lifting: Hierarchical path IDs with arbitrary subtree enumeration.
